api/Invex.Atom.Build.Args.CommandLineArg.summary: Class CommandLineArgs Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Args Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Contains the parsed command-line arguments for an Atom build execution, providing a structured representation of user input. public sealed record CommandLineArgs Inheritance object CommandLineArgs Remarks An instance of this record is created by the Invex.Atom.Build.Args.CommandLineArgsParser after parsing the raw string arguments provided to the Atom application. Constructors CommandLineArgs(bool, IEnumerable<IArg>, IEnumerable<ParseError>?) Contains the parsed command-line arguments for an Atom build execution, providing a structured representation of user input. public CommandLineArgs(bool IsValid, IEnumerable<IArg> Args, IEnumerable<ParseError>? Errors = null) Parameters IsValid bool A value indicating whether the command-line arguments were parsed successfully and are valid. If false, the Atom application will typically terminate or display help. Args IEnumerable<IArg> A read-only list of IArg objects representing the individual arguments parsed from the command line. This list provides access to raw argument objects like HelpArg, CommandArg, or ParamArg. Errors IEnumerable<ParseError> The ParseError objects describing any problems encountered while parsing the raw arguments. When non-empty, IsValid is forced to false. Remarks An instance of this record is created by the Invex.Atom.Build.Args.CommandLineArgsParser after parsing the raw string arguments provided to the Atom application. Properties Args A read-only list of IArg objects representing the individual arguments parsed from the command line. This list provides access to raw argument objects like HelpArg, CommandArg, or ParamArg. public IReadOnlyList<IArg> Args { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<IArg> Commands Gets a read-only list of command arguments (CommandArg) from the command line. public IReadOnlyList<CommandArg> Commands { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<CommandArg> A read-only list of CommandArg objects. Remarks Each CommandArg represents a target to be executed. For atom Clean Build, this list would contain "Clean" and "Build". See Also CommandArg Errors A read-only list of ParseError objects describing any problems encountered while parsing the raw arguments, such as unknown arguments or options that are missing their values. public IReadOnlyList<ParseError> Errors { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<ParseError> Remarks Parsing never throws or writes to the console; errors are collected here and reported by the Atom application after the host is fully constructed, so that all output can be masked for secrets. HasHeadless Gets a value indicating whether the headless argument (-hl or --headless) was provided. public bool HasHeadless { get; } Property Value bool true if the headless argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks This mode is used for non-interactive environments like CI/CD pipelines, where user prompts should be disabled. Running atom MyCommand --headless or atom MyCommand -hl will result in this property being true. See Also HeadlessArg HasHelp Gets a value indicating whether the help argument (-h or --help) was provided. public bool HasHelp { get; } Property Value bool true if the help argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks When this property is true, the Atom application should display help information and exit. Running atom --help or atom -h will result in this property being true. See Also HelpArg IHelpService HasInteractive Gets a value indicating whether the interactive argument (-i or --interactive) was provided. public bool HasInteractive { get; } Property Value bool true if the interactive argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks This flag suggests that the Atom application may prompt the user for input if needed for certain parameters. Running atom MyCommand -i will result in this property being true. See Also InteractiveArg ParamService HasProject Gets a value indicating whether the project argument (-p or --project) was provided. public bool HasProject { get; } Property Value bool true if the project argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks This argument allows specifying a custom Atom project directory, overriding the default. Running atom -p MyAtomProject will result in this property being true. See Also ProjectArg ProjectName HasSkip Gets a value indicating whether the skip argument (-s or --skip) was provided. public bool HasSkip { get; } Property Value bool true if the skip argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks This flag instructs the build executor to skip the execution of dependent targets. Running atom MyTarget --skip or atom MyTarget -s will result in this property being true. See Also SkipArg BuildExecutor HasVerbose Gets a value indicating whether the verbose argument (-v or --verbose) was provided. public bool HasVerbose { get; } Property Value bool true if the verbose argument is present; otherwise, false. Remarks When true, the Atom application should output more detailed logging information for debugging or diagnostics. Running atom MyCommand --verbose or atom MyCommand -v will result in this property being true. See Also VerboseArg IsVerboseEnabled IsValid A value indicating whether the command-line arguments were parsed successfully and are valid. If false, the Atom application will typically terminate or display help. public bool IsValid { get; init; } Property Value bool Params Gets a read-only list of parameter arguments (ParamArg) from the command line. public IReadOnlyList<ParamArg> Params { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<ParamArg> A read-only list of ParamArg objects. Remarks Each ParamArg represents a key-value pair (e.g., --my-param value). For atom --param1 value1, this list would contain one ParamArg object. See Also ParamArg ProjectName Gets the project name specified by the project argument (-p or --project). public string ProjectName { get; } Property Value string The specified project name, or "_atom" if not provided. Remarks If the project argument is not provided, this defaults to "_atom". The Atom project typically resides in a directory with this name. If atom -p MyBuildScripts is run, this property will be "MyBuildScripts". See Also ProjectArg HasProject Methods GetValidationErrors() Gets a list of validation errors for the current command-line arguments. public IReadOnlyList<string> GetValidationErrors() Returns IReadOnlyList<string> A read-only list of error messages. An empty list indicates no validation errors.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IArtifact.title: Interface IArtifactProvider | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IArtifact.summary: Interface IArtifactProvider Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Defines a provider for storing and retrieving build artifacts. public interface IArtifactProvider Remarks Implementations of this interface abstract the underlying storage mechanism, allowing for different backends such as cloud storage or local file systems. The Atom framework uses these providers to manage artifacts for targets like IStoreArtifact and IRetrieveArtifact. Properties OptionalParams Gets a list of parameter names the artifact provider may use but does not always require. IReadOnlyList<string> OptionalParams { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Remarks These are declared as used (not required) parameters of the artifact targets, so that secrets among them are prefetched and injected into generated workflows. Use this for alternatives, such as a connection string or an account URL with a credential, where the provider validates the combination itself. RequiredParams Gets a list of parameter names required by the artifact provider to function correctly. IReadOnlyList<string> RequiredParams { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Remarks These parameters typically include configuration settings or credentials needed to access the artifact storage. Methods Cleanup(IEnumerable<string>, CancellationToken) Deletes all artifacts associated with the specified build run identifiers. Task Cleanup(IEnumerable<string> runIdentifiers, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters runIdentifiers IEnumerable<string> A list of build run identifiers whose artifacts should be deleted. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task A System.Threading.Tasks.Task representing the asynchronous cleanup operation. Remarks This is useful for managing storage by removing old or temporary artifacts. GetStoredRunIdentifiers(string?, string?, CancellationToken) Retrieves a list of all stored run identifiers from the artifact storage. Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> GetStoredRunIdentifiers(string? artifactName = null, string? buildSlice = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters artifactName string An optional artifact name to filter the run identifiers by. buildSlice string An optional build slice to filter the run identifiers by. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> A System.Threading.Tasks.Task<TResult> that completes with a read-only list of stored run identifiers. Remarks This method can be used to list available builds for retrieval or cleanup. RetrieveArtifacts(IEnumerable<string>, string?, string?, CancellationToken) Downloads one or more build artifacts from the configured storage. Task RetrieveArtifacts(IEnumerable<string> artifactNames, string? buildId = null, string? buildSlice = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters artifactNames IEnumerable<string> A list of artifact names to download. buildId string The unique identifier of the build from which to retrieve artifacts. If null, the provider may assume the current run or retrieve the latest version. buildSlice string An optional identifier for a specific build variation to retrieve artifacts from. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task A System.Threading.Tasks.Task representing the asynchronous download operation. StoreArtifacts(IEnumerable<string>, string?, string?, CancellationToken) Uploads one or more build artifacts to the configured storage. Task StoreArtifacts(IEnumerable<string> artifactNames, string? buildId = null, string? buildSlice = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters artifactNames IEnumerable<string> A list of artifact names to upload. Each name typically corresponds to a file or directory. buildId string The unique identifier for the current build. If null, the provider may use a default or environment-provided ID. buildSlice string An optional identifier for a specific build variation (e.g., in a matrix build) to associate the artifacts with. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task A System.Threading.Tasks.Task representing the asynchronous upload operation.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IAtomArti.summary: Interface IAtomArtifactsParam Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Provides a shared parameter for specifying artifact names. public interface IAtomArtifactsParam : IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface defines the AtomArtifacts parameter, which is used by targets like IStoreArtifact and IRetrieveArtifact to identify which artifacts to process. The parameter is typically supplied via the --atom-artifacts command-line argument or an environment variable. Properties AtomArtifacts Gets the names of the artifacts to be processed. [ParamDefinition("atom-artifacts", "The name of the artifact/s to work with, use ',' to separate multiple artifacts", ParamSource.All, null)] string[] AtomArtifacts { get; } Property Value string[] Examples If the command-line argument --atom-artifacts "Package,Symbols" is provided, this property will return ["Package", "Symbols"]. Remarks This parameter specifies which artifacts to store or retrieve. Multiple names can be provided as a comma-separated string, which the framework parses into an array. If no value is provided, it defaults to an empty array.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IRetrieve.title: Interface IRetrieveArtifact | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IRetrieve.summary: Interface IRetrieveArtifact Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Defines a target for retrieving build artifacts using an IArtifactProvider. public interface IRetrieveArtifact : IAtomArtifactsParam, ISetupBuildInfo, IBuildInfo, IVariablesHelper, IReportsHelper, IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IAtomArtifactsParam.AtomArtifacts ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo IBuildInfo.BuildName IBuildInfo.BuildId IBuildInfo.BuildVersion IBuildInfo.BuildTimestamp IBuildInfo.BuildSlice IVariablesHelper.WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) IReportsHelper.AddReportData(IReportData) IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface, when implemented by a build definition, provides the RetrieveArtifact target. It uses the configured IArtifactProvider to download artifacts. Artifacts to be retrieved are specified via the AtomArtifacts parameter. Build information from ISetupBuildInfo (e.g., BuildName, BuildId) is used to identify the correct artifacts to download. This target is hidden by default, primarily for internal use or custom artifact workflows. Properties RetrieveArtifact Defines the target responsible for retrieving artifacts. Target RetrieveArtifact { get; } Property Value Target Remarks This target orchestrates the download of artifacts by invoking the RetrieveArtifacts(IEnumerable<string>, string?, string?, CancellationToken) method. It consumes the AtomArtifacts parameter to determine which artifacts to retrieve and utilizes build metadata from ISetupBuildInfo.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts.IStoreArt.summary: Interface IStoreArtifact Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Artifacts Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Defines a target for storing build artifacts using an IArtifactProvider. public interface IStoreArtifact : IAtomArtifactsParam, ISetupBuildInfo, IBuildInfo, IVariablesHelper, IReportsHelper, IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IAtomArtifactsParam.AtomArtifacts ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo IBuildInfo.BuildName IBuildInfo.BuildId IBuildInfo.BuildVersion IBuildInfo.BuildTimestamp IBuildInfo.BuildSlice IVariablesHelper.WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) IReportsHelper.AddReportData(IReportData) IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface, when implemented by a build definition, provides the StoreArtifact target. It uses the configured IArtifactProvider to upload artifacts. Artifacts to be stored are specified via the AtomArtifacts parameter and are expected to be located in the AtomPublishDirectory. Build information from ISetupBuildInfo (e.g., BuildName, BuildId) is used to categorize or tag the artifacts. This target is hidden by default, primarily for internal use or custom artifact workflows. Properties StoreArtifact Defines the target responsible for storing artifacts. Target StoreArtifact { get; } Property Value Target Remarks This target orchestrates the upload of artifacts by invoking the StoreArtifacts(IEnumerable<string>, string?, string?, CancellationToken) method. It consumes the AtomArtifacts parameter to determine which artifacts to store and utilizes build metadata from ISetupBuildInfo.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.BuildInfo.IBuildInf.title: Interface IBuildInfo | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Build.BuildInfo.IBuildInf.summary: Interface IBuildInfo Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.BuildInfo Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Provides centralized access to essential build metadata, such as version, name, and identifiers. public interface IBuildInfo : IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface defines parameters that supply consistent build information throughout the execution lifecycle. For values that change over time (e.g., BuildTimestamp), it is recommended to consume them from ISetupBuildInfo. This ensures that a stable value is captured at the start of the workflow and reused across all targets, providing consistency. Properties BuildId Gets the unique identifier for the current build run. [ParamDefinition("build-id", "The unique identifier for the build run.", ParamSource.All, null)] string BuildId { get; } Property Value string Remarks This value can be overridden using the --build-id parameter. If not provided, it defaults to the value from the registered IBuildIdProvider. BuildName Gets the human-readable name of the build, derived from the solution or root directory name. [ParamDefinition("build-name", "The name of the build.", ParamSource.All, null)] string BuildName { get; } Property Value string Remarks This value can be overridden using the --build-name parameter. If not provided, it is automatically determined by searching for a .slnx or .sln file in the root directory and using its name. If no solution file is found, it defaults to the name of the root directory. BuildSlice Gets an optional identifier for a specific variation of a build, often used in CI/CD matrix jobs. [ParamDefinition("build-slice", "An identifier for a build variation, used in matrix jobs.", ParamSource.All, null)] string? BuildSlice { get; } Property Value string Remarks This value can be configured using the --build-slice parameter. It is useful for distinguishing between parallel build jobs (e.g., different target frameworks or operating systems). It is null if not specified. BuildTimestamp Gets the build timestamp as a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds). [ParamDefinition("build-timestamp", "The build timestamp in Unix epoch seconds.", ParamSource.All, null)] long BuildTimestamp { get; } Property Value long Remarks This value can be overridden using the --build-timestamp parameter. If not provided, it defaults to the timestamp from the registered IBuildTimestampProvider. Warning: This value may be inconsistent across different process instances. For a stable timestamp, consume this parameter from ISetupBuildInfo so that a consistent value is used across all targets. BuildVersion Gets the semantic version of the build. [ParamDefinition("build-version", "The semantic version of the build.", ParamSource.All, null)] SemVer BuildVersion { get; } Property Value SemVer Remarks This value can be overridden using the --build-version parameter. If not provided, it defaults to the version from the registered IBuildVersionProvider. The value is automatically parsed into a Invex.SemanticVersion.SemVer object.

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Exceptions.CommandL.summary: Class CommandLineException Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Exceptions Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Thrown when command-line arguments are invalid or malformed. public class CommandLineException : AtomException Inheritance object Exception AtomException CommandLineException Examples Example 1: Throwing for an argument-related failure throw new CommandLineException("Parameter 'output' could not be resolved to a valid path.") { ArgumentName = "output" }; Example 2: How to catch and provide user guidance try { await executor.Execute(cancellationToken); } catch (CommandLineException ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Invalid arguments: {ex.Message}"); if (ex.ArgumentName is not null) { Console.WriteLine($"Problematic argument: {ex.ArgumentName}"); } Console.WriteLine("Run with --help for usage information."); Environment.ExitCode = 2; } Remarks This exception signals that build execution cannot proceed because of a problem with the command-line input. This exception provides additional reporting capabilities through custom report data. public sealed class StepFailedException : AtomException Inheritance object Exception AtomException StepFailedException Examples throw new StepFailedException("Could not validate a value"); try { ... } catch (Exception ex) { // It's not recommended to throw a new exception in a catch block without // including the original exception. throw new StepFailedException("An error occurred during the step execution", ex) { ReportData = new TextReportData(...); }; } Remarks This exception is used throughout the Atom framework to signal failures in build targets, such as task execution errors, failed external process calls (via Invex.Process.IProcessRunner), or unmet validation criteria within a target's logic. Consumers of the Atom framework can also throw StepFailedException to programmatically halt a build target and optionally provide custom report data using the ReportData property. The ReportData property allows attaching custom reporting information that can be used for enhanced error reporting, logging, or debugging purposes by Atom's reporting services. This exception inherits from AtomException. Use BuildConfigurationException for configuration errors (duplicate targets, circular dependencies); use StepFailedException for runtime target execution failures. TBuild The type of the build definition, which must derive from BuildDefinition and implement IConfigureHost. Classes generated for BuildDefinitionAttribute do both. Remarks This method performs the following key configurations: Registers the Invex.Atom.Build.AtomService as a hosted service. Registers the build definition (TBuild) and related interfaces. Adds core Atom services like IParamService, IReportService, and Spectre.Console.IAnsiConsole. Registers default providers for build information: IBuildIdProvider, IBuildVersionProvider, and IBuildTimestampProvider. Configures file system access via Invex.FileSystem.IRootedFileSystem. Registers build execution and workflow generation services. Sets up logging with Spectre.Console and report providers, filtering out verbose Microsoft host logs. Parses command-line arguments and makes them available as CommandLineArgs. Resolves and registers the BuildModel. Invokes the static ConfigureHostBuilder(IHostApplicationBuilder) of TBuild, without constructing the build definition, and records ConfigureHost(IHost) for UseAtom(IHost) to call. api/Invex.Atom.Build.ISetupBuildInfo.htm.summary: Interface ISetupBuildInfo Namespace Invex.Atom.Build Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Provides the SetupBuildInfo target, which initializes core build information (name, ID, version, and timestamp) as build variables for consumption by other targets. public interface ISetupBuildInfo : IBuildInfo, IVariablesHelper, IReportsHelper, IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IBuildInfo.BuildName IBuildInfo.BuildId IBuildInfo.BuildVersion IBuildInfo.BuildTimestamp IBuildInfo.BuildSlice IVariablesHelper.WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) IReportsHelper.AddReportData(IReportData) IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Properties SetupBuildInfo Gets the build target responsible for setting up the build ID, version, and timestamp. Target SetupBuildInfo { get; } Property Value Target A Target configured to initialize build information variables and report data. Examples While SetupBuildInfo is often implicitly part of a default build definition, here's how a custom target can depend on it and consume the variables it produces. Variables are consumed via the corresponding build parameters (declared with ConsumesVariable(string, string) and read with GetParam). // In a target interface within your Atom build project public interface IPackage : ISetupBuildInfo { Target Package => t => t .DependsOn(nameof(ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo)) // Ensures build info is set up .ConsumesVariable(nameof(ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo), nameof(BuildVersion)) .Executes(() => { // BuildVersion is resolved from the variable written by SetupBuildInfo Logger.LogInformation("Packaging {Name} version {Version}", BuildName, BuildVersion); // ... further packaging logic ... }); } // To run this build (assuming Atom CLI): // atom Package Remarks The SetupBuildInfo target is a foundational step in the Atom build pipeline. It performs several key actions: Retrieves the build name (from BuildName) and writes it as a build variable named "BuildName". Retrieves the build ID (from BuildId) and writes it as a build variable named "BuildId". Retrieves the build version (from BuildVersion) and writes it as a build variable named "BuildVersion". Retrieves the build timestamp (from BuildTimestamp), converts it to a string, and writes it as a build variable named "BuildTimestamp". Adds a "Run Information" section to the build report, displaying the build name, version, ID, and timestamp. Logs the build ID, version, and timestamp using the configured logger for ISetupBuildInfo. This target is marked as hidden (AsHidden()), meaning it's not typically intended for direct invocation by users but is expected to run as a dependency for other targets or as part of an initial setup sequence. It produces the following build variables, which can be consumed by subsequent targets in the build process: BuildName The name of the build. BuildId The unique identifier for the build execution. BuildVersion The version of the software being built. BuildTimestamp The timestamp of the build (as a string). Successful execution relies on the correct registration and functioning of IBuildIdProvider, IBuildVersionProvider, and IBuildTimestampProvider services within the Atom framework. See Also BuildName WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) AddReportData(IReportData) See Also SetupBuildInfo

Properties ValidateBuild Gets the build target that performs validation checks on the Atom build. Target ValidateBuild { get; } Property Value Target Examples This target is included in BuildDefinition and is automatically available if the build inherits from that type. Otherwise, it can be manually included: public class Build : BuildDefinition { // ... other targets ... // The ValidateBuild target from IValidateBuild would be automatically available // and could be set as a dependency for other targets. api/Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.IDotnetUser.title: Interface IDotnetUserSecrets | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.IDotnetUser.summary: Interface IDotnetUserSecrets Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll An interface that, when implemented on a build definition, enables sourcing secrets from the .NET user secrets store. [ConfigureHostBuilder] public interface IDotnetUserSecrets Examples // 1. Implement the interface in your build definition [BuildDefinition] partial class Build : BuildDefinition, IDotnetUserSecrets, IMyTarget; // 2. Define a secret parameter [SecretDefinition("my-secret", "A secret from user secrets.")] string MySecret => GetParam(() => MySecret); // The value for "my-secret" will now be resolved from the user secrets store. Remarks This interface uses source generation to automatically register the Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.DotnetUserSecretsProvider with the dependency injection container. This allows the IParamService to resolve secrets marked with SecretDefinitionAttribute from the local user secrets store, which is ideal for development-time secrets that should not be committed to source control. This interface is not included in BuildDefinition by default; implement it explicitly on your build definition to enable the user secrets store. The build project also needs a UserSecretsId. Methods ConfigureHostBuilderFromIDotnetUserSecrets(IHostApplicationBuilder) Configures the host builder to register the Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.DotnetUserSecretsProvider. protected static void ConfigureHostBuilderFromIDotnetUserSecrets(IHostApplicationBuilder builder) Parameters builder IHostApplicationBuilder See Also DotnetUserSecretsProvider ISecretsProvider

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.ISecretsPro.title: Interface ISecretsProvider | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets.ISecretsPro.summary: Interface ISecretsProvider Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Secrets Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Defines a contract for retrieving sensitive configuration values (secrets) from a secure storage provider. public interface ISecretsProvider Examples // 1. Implement the interface public class MySecretsProvider : ISecretsProvider { public async ValueTask<string?> GetSecretAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) => await MySecureStore.GetAsync(key, cancellationToken); } // 2. Register the provider from your partial build class static partial void OnConfigureHostBuilder(IHostApplicationBuilder builder) => builder.Services.AddSingleton<ISecretsProvider, MySecretsProvider>(); // 3. Use a secret parameter in a target [SecretDefinition("my-api-key", "An API key.")] string MyApiKey => GetParam(() => MyApiKey); Remarks This interface is the core of the Atom framework's secret management system, enabling secure retrieval of sensitive data like API keys and connection strings. Implementations can integrate with various backends such as Azure Key Vault or .NET User Secrets. The framework automatically discovers and queries registered providers when resolving parameters marked with SecretDefinitionAttribute. Providers are queried in descending Priority order (ties preserve registration order), creating a fallback chain (e.g., from a cloud provider to local user secrets). Before a build executes its targets, Atom asynchronously prefetches the secret parameters used by the targets that will run, passing the build's cancellation token (which is signalled when the host stops). Parameter property getters (GetParam(() => MySecret)) are synchronous, so a secret that was not prefetched (for example, one read by name from a provider or a target that is not part of the run) is resolved by blocking on GetSecretAsync(string, CancellationToken) with System.Threading.CancellationToken.None. Atom runs as a console application without a System.Threading.SynchronizationContext, so this does not deadlock, but implementations should still enforce their own timeouts for network calls. Properties Priority Gets the resolution priority of the secrets provider. int Priority { get; } Property Value int Remarks Providers with a higher priority value are queried first when resolving secrets among multiple providers; providers with equal priority are queried in registration order. The default value is 0. Methods GetSecretAsync(string, CancellationToken) Asynchronously retrieves a secret value by its key. ValueTask<string?> GetSecretAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken) Parameters key string The unique identifier for the secret to retrieve (the parameter's argument name). cancellationToken CancellationToken A token that is cancelled when the build is cancelled or the host is stopping. It is System.Threading.CancellationToken.None when the secret is resolved synchronously outside the prefetch phase. Returns ValueTask<string> The secret value associated with the key, or null if the secret is not found in this provider. Remarks Implementations should return null rather than throwing an exception if a key is not found, allowing the framework to query other registered providers. Results are not cached by the provider contract; Atom caches resolved values in IParamService. See Also SecretDefinitionAttribute IParamService

api/Invex.Atom.Build.Variables.IVariable.summary: Interface IVariableProvider Namespace Invex.Atom.Build.Variables Assembly Invex.Atom.Build.dll Defines a provider for reading and writing workflow variables to a specific storage backend. public interface IVariableProvider Examples public class CustomVariableProvider : IVariableProvider { public async Task<bool> WriteVariable(string variableName, string variableValue, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { // Custom logic to write to an external system return await WriteToExternalSystemAsync(variableName, variableValue); } public async Task<string?> ReadVariable(string jobName, string variableName, CancellationToken cancellationToken) => // Custom logic to read from an external system; null if this provider does not have it await ReadFromExternalSystemAsync(jobName, variableName); } Remarks This interface is part of Atom's extensible variable management system. Multiple providers can be registered, and the IVariableService will delegate operations to them in a chain of responsibility. WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) returns true if the provider handled the write, or false to allow the next provider in the chain to attempt it. ReadVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) returns the variable's value, or null to allow the next provider to attempt it. Methods ReadVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) Reads a variable from the provider's storage system for a specific job context. Task<string?> ReadVariable(string jobName, string variableName, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters jobName string The name of the job context from which to read the variable. variableName string The name of the variable to read. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token. Returns Task<string> A task that resolves to the variable's value, or null if this provider cannot supply it. WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) Writes a variable to the provider's storage system. Task<bool> WriteVariable(string variableName, string variableValue, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters variableName string The name of the variable to write. variableValue string The value to store for the variable. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token. Returns Task<bool> A task that resolves to true if the provider successfully handled the write operation; otherwise, false to delegate to the next provider. See Also IVariableService

api/Invex.Atom.Module.AzureKeyVault.IAzu.title: Interface IAzureKeyVault | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Module.AzureKeyVault.IAzu.summary: Interface IAzureKeyVault Namespace Invex.Atom.Module.AzureKeyVault Assembly Invex.Atom.Module.AzureKeyVault.dll Provides integration with Azure Key Vault for managing secrets and configuration. [ConfigureHostBuilder] public interface IAzureKeyVault : IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface defines the parameters required to connect to an Azure Key Vault and configures the necessary services for retrieving secrets. The vault is accessed with a Microsoft Entra token credential, selected in this order: AzureKeyVaultTenantId, AzureKeyVaultClientId and AzureKeyVaultClientSecret: a client secret credential. AzureKeyVaultTenantId and AzureKeyVaultClientId in a GitHub Actions job with the id-token: write permission: the job's OIDC token, exchanged through a federated credential on the app registration. AzureKeyVaultTenantId, AzureKeyVaultClientId and AzureKeyVaultServiceConnectionId in Azure Pipelines with SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN mapped into the step: a workload identity federation service connection. Otherwise DefaultAzureCredential (environment variables, workload identity, managed identity, Azure CLI, Azure Developer CLI, ...), followed by an interactive browser login when not running headless. Properties AzureKeyVaultAddress Gets the address (URI) of the Azure Key Vault, for example https://my-vault.vault.azure.net/. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-address", "Address (URI) of the Azure Key Vault", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureKeyVaultAddress { get; } Property Value string Remarks This parameter is crucial for identifying which Azure Key Vault instance to connect to. It can be provided via command-line arguments, environment variables, or appsettings.json. AzureKeyVaultAuthPort Gets the port number for the local redirect of the interactive browser login. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-auth-port", "Port for local auth redirect (default 3421). Set to 0 to use a random port.", ParamSource.All, null)] int AzureKeyVaultAuthPort { get; } Property Value int Remarks Only used when no other credential is available and the build is not running headless. The default port is 3421. Setting this to 0 will select a random available port. AzureKeyVaultClientId Gets the client (application) ID of the app registration or user-assigned managed identity that has access to the Azure Key Vault. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-client-id", "Client ID of the app registration or managed identity that has access to the Azure Key Vault", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureKeyVaultClientId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Required for client secret and federated (OIDC) authentication. With DefaultAzureCredential it is used as the workload identity and managed identity client ID. The identity needs permission to get secrets from the vault (for example the Key Vault Secrets User role). AzureKeyVaultClientSecret Gets the client secret of the app registration that has access to the Azure Key Vault. [SecretDefinition("azure-key-vault-client-secret", "Client secret of the app registration that has access to the Azure Key Vault", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureKeyVaultClientSecret { get; } Property Value string Remarks Optional. When set together with AzureKeyVaultTenantId and AzureKeyVaultClientId, client secret authentication is used. Prefer federated credentials (OIDC) in CI where possible. This value is never looked up in the vault itself. AzureKeyVaultServiceConnectionId Gets the ID of the Azure DevOps service connection (workload identity federation) used to authenticate in Azure Pipelines. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-service-connection-id", "Azure DevOps service connection ID for workload identity federation with Azure Key Vault", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureKeyVaultServiceConnectionId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Only used in Azure Pipelines, where SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN must also be mapped into the target step's environment. AzureKeyVaultTenantId Gets the Microsoft Entra tenant ID used to authenticate with the Azure Key Vault. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-tenant-id", "Microsoft Entra tenant ID for Azure Key Vault authentication", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureKeyVaultTenantId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Required for client secret and federated (OIDC) authentication. When set, it also restricts DefaultAzureCredential and interactive login to this tenant. AzureKeyVaultTimeout Gets the timeout, in seconds, for retrieving a single secret from Azure Key Vault, including any authentication that the request triggers. [ParamDefinition("azure-key-vault-timeout", "Timeout in seconds for retrieving a secret from Azure Key Vault (default 120). Set to 0 to disable.", ParamSource.All, null)] int AzureKeyVaultTimeout { get; } Property Value int Remarks The default is 120 seconds, which leaves time to complete an interactive login. Set to 0 to disable the timeout and rely only on the build's cancellation token. AzureKeyVaultValueInjections Configures how Azure Key Vault parameter values are injected into generated workflows. AzureKeyVaultValueInjections AzureKeyVaultValueInjections { get; } Property Value AzureKeyVaultValueInjections Remarks This property allows customization of the source for each Azure Key Vault related parameter. By default, the address, tenant ID and client ID are read from workflow variables, the client secret from the platform's secret store, and the service connection ID is not injected. Methods ConfigureHostBuilderFromIAzureKeyVault(IHostApplicationBuilder) Configures the host builder to add Azure Key Vault services. protected static void ConfigureHostBuilderFromIAzureKeyVault(IHostApplicationBuilder builder) Parameters builder IHostApplicationBuilder The host application builder. Remarks This method registers the Azure Key Vault ISecretsProvider and an IBuildOptionProvider that injects the vault connection parameters into generated workflows. Both implementations are internal to this module.

[ConfigureHostBuilder] public interface IAzureArtifactStorage : IStoreArtifact, IRetrieveArtifact, IAtomArtifactsParam, ISetupBuildInfo, IBuildInfo, IVariablesHelper, IReportsHelper, IBuildAccessor Inherited Members IStoreArtifact.StoreArtifact IRetrieveArtifact.RetrieveArtifact IAtomArtifactsParam.AtomArtifacts ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo IBuildInfo.BuildName IBuildInfo.BuildId IBuildInfo.BuildVersion IBuildInfo.BuildTimestamp IBuildInfo.BuildSlice IVariablesHelper.WriteVariable(string, string, CancellationToken) IReportsHelper.AddReportData(IReportData) IBuildAccessor.GetService<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetServices<T>() IBuildAccessor.GetParam<T>(Expression<Func<T>>, T, Func<string, T>) IBuildAccessor.Services IBuildAccessor.Logger IBuildAccessor.RootedFileSystem IBuildAccessor.ProcessRunner Remarks This interface extends IStoreArtifact and IRetrieveArtifact, enabling the build to both upload and download artifacts from Azure Blob Storage. Connect either with AzureArtifactStorageConnectionString, or with AzureArtifactStorageAccountUrl and a Microsoft Entra token credential, selected in this order: a client secret (tenant ID, client ID and client secret); the GitHub Actions OIDC token (tenant ID and client ID, with the id-token: write permission); an Azure Pipelines workload identity federation service connection (tenant ID, client ID and service connection ID, with SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN mapped); otherwise DefaultAzureCredential, followed by an interactive browser login when not running headless. AzureArtifactStorageClientId Gets the client (application) ID of the app registration or user-assigned managed identity that has access to the storage account. AzureArtifactStorageClientId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Required for client secret and federated (OIDC) authentication with an account URL. With DefaultAzureCredential it is used as the workload identity and managed identity client ID. AzureArtifactStorageClientSecret Gets the client secret of the app registration that has access to the storage account. [SecretDefinition("azurestorage-artifact-client-secret", "Client secret of the app registration that has access to the Azure storage account", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureArtifactStorageClientSecret { get; } Property Value string Remarks Optional; prefer federated credentials (OIDC) in CI where possible. AzureArtifactStorageConnectionString Gets the connection string for the Azure Storage account. [SecretDefinition("azurestorage-artifact-connectionstring", "Connection string for Azure storage container", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureArtifactStorageConnectionString { get; } Property Value string Remarks Optional when AzureArtifactStorageAccountUrl is set; takes precedence over it when both are set. Store it securely, for example as a CI secret, in .NET user secrets or in Azure Key Vault. AzureArtifactStorageContainer Gets the name of the Azure Blob Storage container to use for artifacts. [ParamDefinition("azurestorage-artifact-container", "Azure storage container", ParamSource.All, null)] string AzureArtifactStorageContainer { get; } Property Value string Remarks This parameter specifies the target container within the Azure Storage account where artifacts will be stored and retrieved. AzureArtifactStorageServiceConnectionId Gets the ID of the Azure DevOps service connection (workload identity federation) used to authenticate in Azure Pipelines. [ParamDefinition("azurestorage-artifact-service-connection-id", "Azure DevOps service connection ID for workload identity federation with Azure storage", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureArtifactStorageServiceConnectionId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Only used in Azure Pipelines, where SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN must also be mapped into the target step's environment. AzureArtifactStorageTenantId Gets the Microsoft Entra tenant ID used to authenticate with the storage account. [ParamDefinition("azurestorage-artifact-tenant-id", "Microsoft Entra tenant ID for Azure storage authentication", ParamSource.All, null)] string? AzureArtifactStorageTenantId { get; } Property Value string Remarks Required for client secret and federated (OIDC) authentication with an account URL. ArtifactsPath { get; init; } Property Value string Blame Runs the tests in blame mode. This option is helpful in isolating problematic tests that cause the test host to crash or hang, but it does not create a memory dump by default. When a crash is detected, it creates an sequence file in TestResults/guid/guid_Sequence.xml that captures the order of tests that were run before the crash. Based on the additional settings, hang dump or crash dump can also be collected. Example: Timeout the test run when test takes more than the default timeout of 1 hour, and collect crash dump when the test host exits unexpectedly. (Crash dumps require additional setup, see below.) dotnet test --blame-hang --blame-crash Example: Timeout the test run when a test takes more than 20 minutes and collect hang dump. dotnet test --blame-hang-timeout 20min public bool? Blame { get; init; } Property Value bool? BlameCrash Runs the tests in blame mode and collects a crash dump when the test host exits unexpectedly. This option depends on the version of .NET used, the type of error, and the operating system. For exceptions in managed code, a dump will be automatically collected on .NET 5.0 and later versions. It will generate a dump for testhost or any child process that also ran on .NET 5.0 and crashed. Crashes in native code will not generate a dump. This option works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Crash dumps in native code, or when targetting .NET Framework, or .NET Core 3.1 and earlier versions, can only be collected on Windows, by using Procdump. A directory that contains procdump.exe and procdump64.exe must be in the PATH or PROCDUMP_PATH environment variable. The tools can be downloaded here: https://docs.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/procdump To collect a crash dump from a native application running on .NET 5.0 or later, the usage of Procdump can be forced by setting the VSTEST_DUMP_FORCEPROCDUMP environment variable to 1. api/Invex.Atom.Module.Dotnet.Util.MsBuil.title: Class MsBuildUtil | Atom
api/Invex.Atom.Module.Dotnet.Util.MsBuil.summary: Class MsBuildUtil Namespace Invex.Atom.Module.Dotnet.Util Assembly Invex.Atom.Module.Dotnet.dll Provides utility methods for working with MSBuild project files, specifically for managing version information. public static class MsBuildUtil Inheritance object MsBuildUtil Remarks This utility class offers functionality to manipulate MSBuild project files by updating version-related properties. It ensures consistent version management across different version properties in MSBuild projects. Methods SetVersionInfo(string, SemVer) Updates an MSBuild project file XML with version information from a semantic version. public static string SetVersionInfo(string file, SemVer version) Parameters file string The MSBuild project file content as an XML string. version SemVer The semantic version to apply to the project file. Returns string The updated MSBuild project file content as an XML string with version properties set. Examples var projectXml = File.ReadAllText("MyProject.csproj"); var version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-beta.4"); var updatedXml = MsBuildUtil.SetVersionInfo(projectXml, version); File.WriteAllText("MyProject.csproj", updatedXml); Remarks This method performs the following operations: Removes all existing version-related properties from PropertyGroup elements Creates a new PropertyGroup with standardized version properties Sets Version to the semantic version prefix Sets PackageVersion to the full semantic version Sets AssemblyVersion to the prefix with ".0" appended Sets FileVersion to the prefix with build number from pre-release Sets InformationalVersion to the full semantic version The method removes duplicate version properties to ensure clean project files and consistent versioning. Exceptions XmlException Thrown when the input file content is not valid XML.

api/Invex.Atom.Module.GitHubWorkflows.Ex.summary: Class GitHubWorkflowExpressionExtensions.Expressions Namespace Invex.Atom.Module.GitHubWorkflows.Extensions Assembly Invex.Atom.Module.GitHubWorkflows.dll public sealed class GitHubWorkflowExpressionExtensions.Expressions Inheritance object GitHubWorkflowExpressionExtensions.Expressions Constructors Expressions() public Expressions() Properties Env The env context contains variables that have been set in a workflow, job, or step. It does not contain variables inherited by the runner process. public RawExpression Env { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHub The github context contains information about the workflow run and the event that triggered the run. You can read most of the github context data in environment variables. For more information about environment variables, see Store information in variables. public RawExpression GitHub { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubAction The name of the action currently running, or the id of a step. GitHub removes special characters, and uses the name __run when the current step runs a script without an id. If you use the same action more than once in the same job, the name will include a suffix with the sequence number with underscore before it. For example, the first script you run will have the name __run, and the second script will be named __run_2. Similarly, the second invocation of actions/checkout will be actionscheckout2. public RawExpression GitHubAction { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActionPath The path where an action is located. This property is only supported in composite actions. You can use this path to access files located in the same repository as the action, for example by changing directories to the path (using the corresponding environment variable): cd "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH". For more information on environment variables, see Secure use reference . public RawExpression GitHubActionPath { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActionRef For a step executing an action, this is the ref of the action being executed. For example, v2. public RawExpression GitHubActionRef { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActionRepository For a step executing an action, this is the owner and repository name of the action. For example, actions/checkout. public RawExpression GitHubActionRepository { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActionStatus For a composite action, the current result of the composite action. public RawExpression GitHubActionStatus { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActor The username of the user that triggered the initial workflow run. If the workflow run is a re-run, this value may differ from github.triggering_actor. Any workflow re-runs will use the privileges of github.actor, even if the actor initiating the re-run (github.triggering_actor) has different privileges. public RawExpression GitHubActor { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubActorId The account ID of the person or app that triggered the initial workflow run. For example, 1234567. Note that this is different from the actor username. public RawExpression GitHubActorId { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubApiUrl The URL of the GitHub REST API. public RawExpression GitHubApiUrl { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubBaseRef The base_ref or target branch of the pull request in a workflow run. This property is only available when the event that triggers a workflow run is either pull_request or pull_request_target. public RawExpression GitHubBaseRef { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubEnv Path on the runner to the file that sets environment variables from workflow commands. This file is unique to the current step and is a different file for each step in a job. public RawExpression GitHubEnv { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubEvent The full event webhook payload. You can access individual properties of the event using this context. This object is identical to the webhook payload of the event that triggered the workflow run, and is different for each event. public RawExpression GitHubEvent { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubEventName The name of the event that triggered the workflow run. public RawExpression GitHubEventName { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubEventPath The path to the file on the runner that contains the full event webhook payload. public RawExpression GitHubEventPath { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubGraphqlUrl The URL of the GitHub GraphQL API. public RawExpression GitHubGraphqlUrl { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubHeadRef The head_ref or source branch of the pull request in a workflow run. This property is only available when the event that triggers a workflow run is either pull_request or pull_request_target. public RawExpression GitHubHeadRef { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubJob The job_id of the current job. Note: This context property is set by the Actions runner, and is only available within the execution steps of a job. Otherwise, the value of this property will be null. public RawExpression GitHubJob { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubPath Path on the runner to the file that sets system PATH variables from workflow commands. This file is unique to the current step and is a different file for each step in a job. public RawExpression GitHubPath { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRef The fully-formed ref of the branch or tag that triggered the workflow run. For branches the format is refs/heads/<branch_name>. For pull requests events except pull_request_target that were not merged, it is refs/pull/<pr_number>/merge. For tags it is refs/tags/<tag_name>. For example, refs/heads/feature-branch-1. public RawExpression GitHubRef { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRefName The short ref name of the branch or tag that triggered the workflow run. This value matches the branch or tag name shown on GitHub. For example, feature-branch-1. For pull requests that were not merged, the format is <pr_number>/merge. public RawExpression GitHubRefName { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRefProtected true if branch protections or rulesets are configured for the ref that triggered the workflow run. public RawExpression GitHubRefProtected { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRefType The type of ref that triggered the workflow run. Valid values are branch or tag. public RawExpression GitHubRefType { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRepository The owner and repository name. For example, octocat/Hello-World. public RawExpression GitHubRepository { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRepositoryId The ID of the repository. For example, 123456789. Note that this is different from the repository name. public RawExpression GitHubRepositoryId { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRepositoryOwner The repository owner's username. For example, octocat. public RawExpression GitHubRepositoryOwner { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRepositoryOwnerId The repository owner's account ID. For example, 1234567. Note that this is different from the owner's name. public RawExpression GitHubRepositoryOwnerId { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRepositoryUrl The Git URL to the repository. For example, git://github.com/octocat/hello-world.git. public RawExpression GitHubRepositoryUrl { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRetentionDays The number of days that workflow run logs and artifacts are kept. public RawExpression GitHubRetentionDays { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRunAttempt A unique number for each attempt of a particular workflow run in a repository. This number begins at 1 for the workflow run's first attempt, and increments with each re-run. public RawExpression GitHubRunAttempt { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRunId A unique number for each workflow run within a repository. This number does not change if you re-run the workflow run. public RawExpression GitHubRunId { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubRunNumber A unique number for each run of a particular workflow in a repository. This number begins at 1 for the workflow's first run, and increments with each new run. This number does not change if you re-run the workflow run. public RawExpression GitHubRunNumber { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubSecretSource The source of a secret used in a workflow. Possible values are None, Actions, Codespaces, or Dependabot. public RawExpression GitHubSecretSource { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubServerUrl The URL of the GitHub server. For example: https://github.com. public RawExpression GitHubServerUrl { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubSha The commit SHA that triggered the workflow. The value of this commit SHA depends on the event that triggered the workflow. For example, ffac537e6cbbf934b08745a378932722df287a53. public RawExpression GitHubSha { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubToken A token to authenticate on behalf of the GitHub App installed on your repository. This is functionally equivalent to the GITHUB_TOKEN secret. Note: This context property is set by the Actions runner, and is only available within the execution steps of a job. Otherwise, the value of this property will be null. public RawExpression GitHubToken { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubTriggeringActor The username of the user that initiated the workflow run. If the workflow file doesn't specify a name, the value of this property is the full path of the workflow file in the repository. public RawExpression GitHubWorkflow { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubWorkflowRef The ref path to the workflow. For example, octocat/hello-world/.github/workflows/my-workflow.yml@refs/heads/my_branch. public RawExpression GitHubWorkflowRef { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubWorkflowSha The commit SHA for the workflow file. public RawExpression GitHubWorkflowSha { get; } Property Value RawExpression GitHubWorkspace The default working directory on the runner for steps, and the default location of your repository when using the checkout action. public RawExpression GitHubWorkspace { get; } Property Value RawExpression Inputs This context is only available in a reusable workflow or in a workflow triggered by the workflow_dispatch event. You can access this context from any job or step in a workflow. This object contains the properties listed below. public RawExpression Inputs { get; } Property Value RawExpression Job This context changes for each job in a workflow run. You can access this context from any step in a job. This object contains all the properties listed below. public RawExpression Job { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobCheckRunId The check run ID of the current job. public RawExpression JobCheckRunId { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobContainer Information about the job's container. public RawExpression JobContainer { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobContainerId The ID of the container. public RawExpression JobContainerId { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobContainerNetwork The ID of the container network. The runner creates the network used by all containers in a job. public RawExpression JobContainerNetwork { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobServices The service containers created for a job. public RawExpression JobServices { get; } Property Value RawExpression JobStatus The current status of the job. Possible values are success, failure, or cancelled. public RawExpression JobStatus { get; } Property Value RawExpression Jobs This is only available in reusable workflows, and can only be used to set outputs for a reusable workflow. This object contains all the properties listed below. public RawExpression Jobs { get; } Property Value RawExpression Matrix This context is only available for jobs in a matrix, and changes for each job in a workflow run. You can access this context from any job or step in a workflow. This object contains the properties listed below. public RawExpression Matrix { get; } Property Value RawExpression Needs This context is only populated for workflow runs that have dependent jobs, and changes for each job in a workflow run. You can access this context from any job or step in a workflow. This object contains all the properties listed below. public RawExpression Needs { get; } Property Value RawExpression Runner This context changes for each job in a workflow run. Inheritance object BuildCache<T> Remarks Keys are compared by their default equality, which for build definitions and helpers is reference equality. The cache is thread-safe and holds its entries for the lifetime of the cache instance, so typically it is stored in a static readonly field. Typical use is to compute an expensive per-build value once, e.g. via GetOrAdd(IBuildAccessor, Func<IBuildAccessor, T>). Constructors BuildCache() public BuildCache() Methods Clear() Removes all keys and values from the cache. public void Clear() GetOrAdd(IBuildAccessor, Func<IBuildAccessor, T>) Gets the value associated with the specified key, or adds one created by valueFactory if the key is not present. public T GetOrAdd(IBuildAccessor key, Func<IBuildAccessor, T> valueFactory) Parameters key IBuildAccessor The key of the value to get or add. valueFactory Func<IBuildAccessor, T> The function used to create the value when the key is not present. Returns T The existing or newly created value. Remarks Under concurrent access valueFactory may be invoked more than once for the same key, but only one result is stored and returned to all callers. Remove(IBuildAccessor) Removes the value associated with the specified key from the cache. public bool Remove(IBuildAccessor key) Parameters key IBuildAccessor The key of the value to remove. Returns bool true if the key was found and removed; otherwise, false. Set(IBuildAccessor, T) Adds or updates a value in the cache with the provided key. public T Set(IBuildAccessor key, T value) Parameters key IBuildAccessor The key of the value to set. value T The value to associate with the key. Returns T The value that was set. TryGetValue(IBuildAccessor, out T) Attempts to get the value associated with the specified key from the cache. public bool TryGetValue(IBuildAccessor key, out T result) Parameters key IBuildAccessor The key of the value to get. result T When this method returns, contains the object from the cache that has the specified key, or the default value of the type if the operation failed. Returns bool true if the key was found in the cache; otherwise, false.

api/Invex.Atom.Workflows.WorkflowOutdate.summary: Class WorkflowOutdatedException Namespace Invex.Atom.Workflows Assembly Invex.Atom.Workflows.dll Thrown when workflow files are out of date in headless mode. public class WorkflowOutdatedException : AtomException Inheritance object Exception AtomException WorkflowOutdatedException Examples Typical CI/CD failure scenario and resolution: // In CI/CD pipeline, the build fails with: // "One or more workflows are out of date. To regenerate workflows, run the 'Gen' target." // To fix locally: // 1. Run: dotnet run --project _atom Gen // 2. Commit the regenerated workflow files // 3. Push to repository Remarks This exception is thrown when the build is running in headless mode (typically in CI/CD environments) and the workflow files are detected to be out of date. In headless mode, the build does not automatically regenerate workflow files to prevent unexpected changes in automated environments. Headless mode is typically enabled with the --headless flag and is used in CI/CD pipelines to ensure reproducibility and prevent unintended modifications to workflow files. To resolve this error, run the Gen target (see Gen) to regenerate the workflow files, then commit the updated files to your repository. docs/built-in-targets/generate-workflow-.title: Gen (Generate Workflow Files) | Atom
docs/built-in-targets/generate-workflow-.summary: Gen (Generate Workflow Files) The Gen target generates CI/CD configuration files from your workflow definitions. Every workflow build has it; run it after changing targets or workflows. Interface: IGen · Package: Invex.Atom.Workflows What It Does Resolves each WorkflowDefinition in your build's Workflows property. Analyses the target dependency graph, artifact dependencies, and variable dependencies. Maps targets into jobs and creates a platform-neutral WorkflowModel. Invokes each registered IWorkflowWriter (one per platform type) to render and write the YAML files. Generated File Locations Platform Output Directory GitHub Actions .github/workflows/ Azure DevOps .devops/workflows/ Usage dotnet run --project _atom Gen # or, with the atom global tool atom Gen Requirements Your build must: Implement IWorkflowBuildDefinition (or derive from WorkflowBuildDefinition). Define IWorkflowBuildDefinition.Workflows with at least one definition. Interface builds explicitly implement the property; partial classes override it. Inherit a platform module interface (IGitHubWorkflows, IDevOpsWorkflows, or both) so the corresponding workflow writer is registered. Automatic Generation & Outdated File Detection You usually don't need to run Gen explicitly during local development: when the build runs in interactive (non-headless) mode, the WorkflowLifecycleHook regenerates workflow files automatically before any targets execute. When the build runs in headless mode (the --headless flag, typical in CI), files are not regenerated. Instead, if the files on disk are out of date with the current definitions, the build fails early with a WorkflowOutdatedException, prompting you to run the Gen target locally and commit the regenerated files. See also Workflow Definitions: what Gen generates from. Debugging Workflows: inspect the resolved model. IGen WorkflowOutdatedException

docs/built-in-targets/setup-build-info.h.summary: SetupBuildInfo The SetupBuildInfo target initialises the build's identity — name, ID, version, and timestamp — and makes them available as workflow variables. Include it in workflows whose later targets need the build version or ID. Interface: ISetupBuildInfo · Package: Invex.Atom.Build What It Does Reads BuildName, BuildId, BuildVersion, and BuildTimestamp from the registered build info providers. Writes each as a workflow variable: BuildName, BuildId, BuildVersion, BuildTimestamp. Adds a "Run Information" section to the build report. Logs the values. Produced Variables Variable Description BuildName The logical name of the build BuildId Unique identifier for this run BuildVersion Semantic version string BuildTimestamp Timestamp as a string Usage Include SetupBuildInfo as a dependency of your first workflow target: public override IReadOnlyList<WorkflowDefinition> Workflows => [ new("CI") { Targets = [ new(nameof(ISetupBuildInfo.SetupBuildInfo)), new(nameof(Compile)), new(nameof(Test)), ], // ... }, ]; Visibility This target is marked as hidden — it doesn't appear in default help output but is still executable. See also Build Info: the providers behind each value. Variables: consuming the produced variables. ISetupBuildInfo

docs/built-in-targets/validate-build.htm.title: ValidateBuild | Atom
docs/built-in-targets/validate-build.htm.summary: ValidateBuild The ValidateBuild target checks the Atom build configuration for common issues. Run it to catch configuration mistakes, such as undocumented targets, before they reach CI. Interface: IValidateBuild · Package: Invex.Atom.Build What It Does Inspects all targets in the build model. Reports warnings for targets without descriptions. Reports errors for critical configuration problems (extensible). Adds warning/error lists to the build report. Throws StepFailedException if any errors are found. Usage Run directly: dotnet run -- ValidateBuild Or include as a dependency: Target MyTarget => t => t .DependsOn(nameof(IValidateBuild.ValidateBuild)) .Executes(() => { /* ... */ }); Output Warnings appear in the build report. Example: Warnings: - Target 'MyTarget' has no description. See also Targets: describing targets with DescribedAs. IValidateBuild StepFailedException

docs/core-concepts/artifacts.html.title: Artifacts | Atom
docs/core-concepts/artifacts.html.summary: Artifacts Artifacts are files or directories produced by one target and consumed by another. Atom tracks artifact dependencies to ensure correct execution order, especially in workflow scenarios where different targets may run on different machines. You need them when one target's output files are another target's input. Producing Artifacts Declare that a target produces an artifact: Target Pack => t => t .DescribedAs("Packs NuGet packages") .ProducesArtifact("packages") .Executes(async () => { // write files to the artifact directory }); You can produce multiple artifacts: .ProducesArtifacts(["packages", "binaries"]) Consuming Artifacts Declare that a target consumes an artifact from another target: Target Deploy => t => t .ConsumesArtifact(nameof(Pack), "packages") .Executes(async () => { // read files from the artifact directory }); Multiple artifacts from the same or different targets: .ConsumesArtifacts(nameof(Pack), ["packages", "binaries"]) Build Slices Artifacts can be scoped to a build slice — a named variation within a matrix build (e.g. a specific OS or framework): .ProducesArtifact("tool", buildSlice: "windows-x64") .ConsumesArtifact(nameof(PackTool), "tool", buildSlice: "windows-x64") You can also consume an artifact across all slices: .ConsumesArtifact(nameof(PackTool), "tool", buildSlices: ["windows-x64", "linux-x64"]) IArtifactProvider When targets run on separate CI jobs, artifacts must be transported between machines. By default, workflows use the CI platform's native artifact mechanism (e.g. actions/upload-artifact on GitHub Actions). Alternatively, you can register an IArtifactProvider and enable it with the UseCustomArtifactProvider workflow option (BuildOptions.Artifacts.UseCustomProvider), which routes artifacts through the hidden StoreArtifact / RetrieveArtifact targets instead: Interface Package Storage IAzureArtifactStorage Invex.Atom.Module.AzureStorage Azure Blob Storage Locally, artifacts are simply directories under the Atom publish/artifacts paths — no provider is required. Provider API public interface IArtifactProvider { Task StoreArtifacts(IEnumerable<string> artifactNames, ...); Task RetrieveArtifacts(IEnumerable<string> artifactNames, ...); Task Cleanup(IEnumerable<string> runIdentifiers, ...); Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> GetStoredRunIdentifiers(...); } Next steps Variables: share string values instead of files. Azure Storage: store artifacts in Azure Blob Storage. IArtifactProvider IStoreArtifact IRetrieveArtifact

docs/core-concepts/build-definitions.htm.title: Build Definitions | Atom
docs/core-concepts/build-definitions.htm.summary: Build Definitions A build definition is the central entry point for an Atom build. It declares which targets exist, what parameters are available, and how the build host is configured. For consumer builds, the recommended approach is an interface that extends IBuildDefinition; use a partial class when the build needs class-specific host configuration. Recommended: interface-based builds Define the build as an interface annotated with [BuildDefinition] and [GenerateEntryPoint]: [BuildDefinition] [GenerateEntryPoint] internal interface IBuild : IBuildDefinition { Target SayHello => t => t .DescribedAs("Prints a greeting") .Executes(() => Logger.LogInformation("Hello, World!")); } This pattern is recommended because the build can compose targets, parameters, and host configuration from module interfaces without putting all implementation in one type. The generated entry point discovers the interface members and runs the build. Alternative: partial class builds Use a partial class when the build itself needs class members, such as the optional OnConfigureHostBuilder host hook (an interface-based build can add them to its generated partial class Build instead): [BuildDefinition] [GenerateEntryPoint] internal partial class Build : BuildDefinition { Target SayHello => t => t .DescribedAs("Prints a greeting") .Executes(() => Logger.LogInformation("Hello, World!")); } The class must be partial so source generators can augment it, and it must derive from BuildDefinition or WorkflowBuildDefinition. It can also implement module interfaces in the same way as an interface-based build. What the Source Generator Does When you apply [BuildDefinition], the Atom source generator automatically: Discovers all Target properties (including those from implemented interfaces) and populates the TargetDefinitions dictionary. Discovers all [ParamDefinition] / [SecretDefinition] properties and populates the ParamDefinitions dictionary. Generates the AccessParam method so the framework can inspect parameter values. This means you never need to manually register targets or parameters — just declare them and the generator wires everything up. [GenerateEntryPoint] Adding this attribute causes the source generator to emit a Program.cs with a Main method: // Auto-generated AtomHost.Run<Build>(args); If you need custom host configuration, omit [GenerateEntryPoint] and write your own entry point: var builder = AtomHost.CreateAtomBuilder<Build>(args); // customise builder.Services, builder.Configuration, etc. builder.Build().UseAtom().Run(); Composing module interfaces Targets and parameters are typically defined in interfaces so they can be shared across builds or published in module packages: public interface IMyTargets : IBuildAccessor { [ParamDefinition("greeting", "The greeting message")] string Greeting => GetParam(() => Greeting, "Hello"); Target SayGreeting => t => t .DescribedAs("Says a greeting") .Executes(() => Logger.LogInformation(Greeting)); } [BuildDefinition] [GenerateEntryPoint] internal partial class Build : BuildDefinition, IMyTargets { } The source generator discovers SayGreeting and Greeting from IMyTargets and includes them in the build model. [GenerateSolutionModel] When applied alongside [BuildDefinition], this attribute generates a typed model of your solution's projects, giving you compile-time access to project paths. OnConfigureHostBuilder / OnConfigureHost Implement the optional static partial method OnConfigureHostBuilder on your build class to register additional services before the build runs, and OnConfigureHost to configure the built host: static partial void OnConfigureHostBuilder(IHostApplicationBuilder builder) => builder.Services.AddSingleton<IMyService, MyService>(); They run after the hooks of the module interfaces the build implements, without constructing the build definition. See Hosting for details, including interface-based builds. Caching per-build values BuildCache<T> is a thread-safe cache keyed by an IBuildAccessor (typically the build definition), for values that are expensive to compute and should be computed once per build: private static readonly BuildCache<string> ChangelogCache = new(); string Changelog => ChangelogCache.GetOrAdd(this, _ => File.ReadAllText("CHANGELOG.md")); Keys use reference equality, and entries live as long as the cache instance. Use Set, TryGetValue, Remove and Clear for explicit control. Next steps Targets: define the units of work in a build. Hosting: entry points and host configuration. Source Generators: what the generators emit. BuildDefinitionAttribute IBuildDefinition BuildDefinition

docs/core-concepts/build-info.html.title: Build Info | Atom
docs/core-concepts/build-info.html.summary: Build Info Atom provides a pluggable system for determining the build's identity: its name, ID, version, and timestamp. Read this when you need to version packages or identify a build run. IBuildInfo The IBuildInfo interface exposes the following parameters. Each can be overridden on the command line (e.g. --build-name, --build-id, --build-version, --build-timestamp, --build-slice): Property Type Description BuildName string Logical name of the build (defaults to the solution file or root directory) BuildId string Unique identifier for this build run BuildVersion SemVer Semantic version of the build BuildTimestamp long Build timestamp in Unix epoch seconds BuildSlice string? Optional identifier for a build variation in matrix jobs Providers Each piece of build info is resolved by a dedicated provider interface: Interface Default Description IBuildIdProvider DefaultBuildIdProvider Combines the build version and timestamp (e.g. "1.2.3-1672531200") IBuildVersionProvider DefaultBuildVersionProvider Parses version properties from Directory.Build.props; falls back to 1.0.0 IBuildTimestampProvider DefaultBuildTimestampProvider Returns the current time as Unix epoch seconds Replacing a Provider Register your own implementation in the DI container. For example, the GitVersion module replaces both the ID and version providers: builder.Services .AddSingleton<IBuildIdProvider, GitVersionBuildIdProvider>() .AddSingleton<IBuildVersionProvider, GitVersionBuildVersionProvider>(); SetupBuildInfo Target The built-in ISetupBuildInfo interface provides a SetupBuildInfo target that: Reads the build name, ID, version, and timestamp from the providers. Writes each as a workflow variable (BuildName, BuildId, BuildVersion, BuildTimestamp). Adds a "Run Information" section to the build report. Logs the values. Most builds include SetupBuildInfo as a dependency of their first real target. See SetupBuildInfo for details. Next steps Build Options: configure build behaviour. SetupBuildInfo: the target that publishes build info as variables. GitVersion: derive the ID and version from Git history. IBuildInfo IBuildIdProvider IBuildVersionProvider IBuildTimestampProvider

docs/core-concepts/build-options.html.title: Build Options | Atom
docs/core-concepts/build-options.html.summary: Build Options Build options are configuration flags that modify the behaviour of the build or workflow at definition time. You use them to switch module features on and to tune individual workflow targets. IBuildOption All build options implement the marker interface IBuildOption. Options can be applied at three levels: Build-wide — via the Options property on your build definition Workflow-wide — via WorkflowDefinition.Options Per-target — via WorkflowTargetDefinition.Options public override IReadOnlyList<IBuildOption> Options => [ BuildOptions.GitVersion.ProvideBuildId, BuildOptions.GitVersion.ProvideBuildVersion, ]; ToggleBuildOption A simple on/off option: BuildOptions.Target.SuppressArtifactPublishing Common Options Options are accessed via the static BuildOptions class, which is extended by modules.
